name: Agent-Managed Memory
question: Should the agent decide what to remember?
summary: Give the agent tools to view, write, search and edit its own memory, and let it decide when to use them. MemGPT framed this as an operating system paging data between a small main context and larger stores. The agent can then resume long tasks across sessions, but every path and write must be checked.
useCases: Multi-day tasks that must resume where they stopped
Agents whose useful notes are hard to predict in advance
Workflows where the agent keeps checklists or progress files

steps.title: Declare the memory tool
steps.text: memory_20250818 is a client-side tool. Claude sends view, create, str_replace, insert, delete and rename commands; your code stores the files.

steps.title: Implement the handlers
steps.text: Map each command onto your own storage: a folder, a database or object storage, per tenant and client.

steps.title: Validate every path
steps.text: Resolve the path first, then check it is still inside the memory root. /memories/../config.env resolves outside and is refused.

steps.title: Run the loop
steps.text: The agent views its memory first, finds progress.md at item 12 of 30, resumes at 13 and updates the file as it goes.

steps.title: Pair with context editing
steps.text: Clearing old tool results keeps each session small. Before results are cleared, the agent can save what matters to memory.

steps.title: Log and review writes
steps.text: Every write is logged with its path, so a person can review what the agent chose to remember.

library.what: memory_20250818 is a client-side tool: Claude issues view, create, str_replace, insert, delete and rename commands and your code stores the files.

practice.note: Run the usual tool loop: pass each memory tool_use block to handle() and return its result. Log every write for review.

samples.code:
from pathlib import Path
import anthropic

ROOT = Path("./memories").resolve()
client = anthropic.Anthropic()

def safe(p: str) -> Path:
    full = (ROOT / p.removeprefix("/memories").lstrip("/")).resolve()
    if not full.is_relative_to(ROOT):                  # resolve first, then check
        raise ValueError("path outside /memories")
    return full

def handle(cmd: dict) -> str:
    if cmd["command"] == "view":
        p = safe(cmd["path"])
        return "\n".join(x.name for x in p.iterdir()) if p.is_dir() else p.read_text()
    if cmd["command"] == "create":
        p = safe(cmd["path"]); p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        p.write_text(cmd["file_text"]); return "saved"
    ...                                                # str_replace, insert, delete, rename

r = client.beta.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-4-5", max_tokens=2048,        # use your current model
    betas=["context-management-2025-06-27"],
    tools=[{"type": "memory_20250818", "name": "memory"}],
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Continue the ITR checklist for client 114."}])

numericDrill.question: Without memory, each of 3 sessions re-reads everything: 160k tokens each. With memory, session 1 costs 90k and sessions 2 and 3 cost 60k each. What percentage of tokens is saved?

interview.question: Why is a startswith check not enough for memory paths?
interview.answer: A path like /memories/../secrets.txt starts with /memories but resolves outside it. Resolve the full path first, including symlinks, then check that it stays inside the memory root.

interview.question: When would you not give the agent memory tools?
interview.answer: When writes must be predictable and auditable, as in regulated customer data. A developer-run pipeline with a fixed schema and policy is easier to test and review than an agent deciding what to store.

mistakes.mistake: Validating paths with a string prefix
mistakes.fix: Resolve, then check the root; reject symlinks out

mistakes.mistake: Letting the agent write without logs
mistakes.fix: Log every write and review a sample

quiz.question: A memory handler checks path.startswith("/memories"). Which path wrongly passes?
quiz.explanation: It starts with /memories but resolves outside; resolve first, then check the root.

quiz.question: Which commands does Claude’s memory tool (memory_20250818) support? Select all that apply.
quiz.explanation: It supports view, create, str_replace, insert, delete and rename; there is no execute.

quiz.question: Where are the memory tool’s files stored?

quiz.question: Three sessions cost 160k each without memory. With memory they cost 90k, 60k and 60k. What percentage is saved?
Which paper framed agent-managed memory as an operating system paging between a small main context and larger stores?
quiz.explanation: MemGPT introduced virtual context management with memory tiers.

quiz.question: Which make memory tool handlers safer? Select all that apply.
options: Resolve the path, then check it is inside the root
quiz.explanation: Resolved-path checks and tenant isolation help; unrestricted symlinks and no logs are unsafe.

quiz.question: An agent writes progress every 5 items. A session ends after item 12. Where does the next session resume?
quiz.explanation: The last saved checkpoint is item 10, so it resumes at item 11 and redoes 11 and 12.

quiz.question: In Anthropic’s evaluation, memory tool plus context editing improved performance by about how much over baseline?
quiz.explanation: Anthropic reported a 39% improvement with both; 84% was the token reduction from context editing.

quiz.question: When is agent-managed memory a poor fit?
options: Regulated customer data where every write must follow a fixed schema
quiz.explanation: Predictable, auditable writes favour a developer-run pipeline.

quiz.question: A session fits 16 items. The agent writes progress every item. How many sessions does a 30-item checklist need?
quiz.explanation: 16 + 14 = 30, so two sessions.

quiz.question: Letta memory blocks have which properties? Select all that apply.
options: A description that guides the agent
quiz.explanation: Blocks have a label, value, limit and description; there is no GPU field.

quiz.question: Which Letta tools let an agent write to and search archival memory?
quiz.explanation: Letta’s archival memory uses archival_memory_insert and archival_memory_search.

quiz.question: Python: (ROOT / "../config.env").resolve() lands outside ROOT. Which check catches it?
quiz.explanation: Resolve first, then test containment with is_relative_to.

quiz.question: Why pair the memory tool with context editing?
options: The agent can save key information before old tool results are cleared
quiz.explanation: Claude is warned near the clearing threshold and can save what matters to memory first.

quiz.question: A clinic agent can write its own memory. Which risks need controls? Select all that apply.
options: Writing patient health details into notes
Storing instructions that change its future behaviour
Reading its progress file at session start
quiz.explanation: Sensitive data and injected instructions need filters and review; reading progress and resuming are the intended use.

quiz.question: Each item costs 7k tokens, start-up 4k and each progress write 1k. A session does 16 items and writes 3 times. What does it cost?
What should the agent do first in a new session with the memory tool?
quiz.explanation: Viewing memory first is what lets it resume progress.

quiz.question: A path /memories/clients/../progress.md is requested. After resolving, where does it point?
quiz.explanation: clients/.. cancels out, leaving /memories/progress.md, which is inside the root.

quiz.question: Which belong in a review process for agent-written memory? Select all that apply.
options: Logging every write with its path
Letting the agent approve its own writes
quiz.explanation: Logs and sampling support review; self-approval and deleting logs defeat it.

quiz.question: Progress is written every 10 items; sessions fit 16. Starting at item 1, how many items are redone across sessions 1 and 2?
quiz.explanation: Session 1 does 1–16 and saves 10; session 2 restarts at 11, redoing 11–16: 6 items.
